a1
Joseph presented his brothers to Pharaoh. They said: we are shepherds, and the famine in Canaan is severe.
a2
Pharaoh told Joseph: settle them in Goshen, the best of the land.
b1
Then Joseph brought in Jacob, who blessed Pharaoh. Pharaoh asked: how old are you?
b2
Jacob said: a hundred and thirty years. Few and hard have been my years.
c1
The famine grew heavy. The people paid for grain with silver, then livestock, then land and themselves.
c2
Joseph bought the land for Pharaoh and gave the people seed. A fifth of the harvest would be Pharaoh's. They said: you have saved our lives.
d1
Israel settled in Goshen, gained property, and grew very numerous.
d2
Jacob lived in Egypt seventeen years. Near death, he said to Joseph: do not bury me in Egypt. Carry me to my fathers.
e1
Joseph swore it. And Israel bowed at the head of his bed.
h1
Jacob called his life a journey, with years few and hard.
h2
Yet he blessed a king, and asked to be carried home to his fathers.
h3
Hard years do not waste a life that walks toward a promise.
h4
Today, hold your troubles loosely, and keep walking.
i
What are you really walking toward today?
